papers.title: Self-organizing reinforcement learning: a learner-free swarm approaches the explore-exploit optimum
papers.abstract: The explore/exploit trade-off is the core problem of reinforcement learning (RL). We show that a minimal foraging swarm approaches its optimum - the ideal-free / Nash allocation of a multi-agent resource-sharing game (an equilibrium, not a return maximum) - with no learner and no reward signal. Agents explore by heavy-tailed (Levy) flights, recruit neighbours to a discovery through a threshold cascade on their proximity network, and disperse as a patch crowds; this cascade cycle balances exploration and exploitation and drives foragers toward the ideal free distribution. The swarm attains the shape of this optimum (committed foragers track richness with slope 0.94) but not its exact equilibrium - it stays measurably exploitable - reaching it dynamically (~150 steps) through the coupling of recruitment to movement: remove the coupling and matching collapses (0.94 -> 0.08). The RL sits at the level of the problem and the allocation reached, not the micro-rule: no step evaluates payoff (reward-free by construction, though the crowd signal is informationally tied to payoff), and the swarm reaches the allocation without learning it (quality plateaus and re-settles after resources move, no cumulative gain). Against a trained baseline the comparison is two-sided: in an easier, disembodied game a learner is more precise, while in the same embodied environment the reward-free swarm reaches ~65% of a validated oracle ceiling at zero training and leads until trained PPO and centralised-critic (CTDE) learners overtake it (~74-75%, 16 seeds, all above the swarm mean) after ~4,000 of 15,000 training steps - its advantage is in budget, not asymptote. In this one setting we read it not as beating RL but as a strong zero-shot, reward-free operating point: a demonstration that the self-organizing physics of a minimal swarm can carry a collective close to the optimum RL seeks, with none of RL's machinery.

papers.title: Scaling H2 Factorization to Billion-Unknown Three-Dimensional Problems
papers.abstract: Strong recursive skeletonization provides approximate direct solvers for dense matrices from integral equations and kernel methods, but distributed implementations face substantial communication costs and limited parallelism, especially in three dimensions. We present a distributed-memory $\mathcal{H}^2$ factorization solver for symmetric matrices that combines spatial box coloring, delayed Schur complement updates, streamed sketching-based interpolative decomposition, and BLAS-3 and shared-memory kernels. Spatial coloring enables every process to participate in each boundary stage, while delayed updates and streamed sketching reduce dense storage and communication. To our knowledge, this is the first distributed-memory strong recursive skeletonization factorization demonstrated for three-dimensional volume integral equations at billion-unknown scale. Experiments on up to 512 compute nodes demonstrate factorization of a three-dimensional Laplace system with 3.62 billion unknowns, alongside three-dimensional Helmholtz tests and a two-dimensional Mat\'ern system with 268 million unknowns. Combining streamed sketching and fully delayed updates reduces factorization time by $6.9\times$ for Laplace and $8.5\times$ for Helmholtz relative to the unsketched, eager configuration, while reducing maximum per-process resident memory by 57\% and 54\%, respectively.

papers.title: Quantum f-divergences from retrodiction: a unifying classical variational principle
papers.abstract: The same classical f-divergence admits inequivalent extensions to quantum states. The question is whether these extensions can be obtained from a common operational variational principle. Here we generalize Matsumoto's reverse-test optimization by introducing a reference prior state. More explicitly, we minimize the statistical distinguishability between a forward and a reverse prepare-and-measure process, related by retrodiction through the chosen reference and subject to prescribed quantum averages. Distinguishability is quantified by the classical f-divergence between their complete records. For faithful states in finite dimension, we prove that the same spectral implementation attains the minimum simultaneously for every operator-convex f. Varying the reference allows us to interpolate between standard and maximal quantum f-divergences of the prescribed states, passing through the geodesic family. More precisely, a flat reference yields the standard quantum f-divergences, thereby giving the Nussbaum-Szko{\l}a distributions a variational characterization as optimal records. Choosing either prescribed state as reference recovers maximal quantum f-divergences and Matsumoto's reverse tests, while power references realize the geodesic interpolation. In the relative-entropy case, this gives the passage from Umegaki to Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy by changing the prior for retrodiction.

papers.title: Families of relative periodic orbits in the planar three-body problem via consecutive alignments
papers.abstract: Relative periodic orbits (RPOs) are solutions of the three-body problem that are periodic in a uniformly rotating reference frame and, in general, quasi-periodic in inertial coordinates. We present a numerical procedure for computing and continuing one-parameter families of RPOs of the planar Newtonian three-body problem. The method exploits consecutive syzygies, understood here as configurations in which the three bodies are aligned and their velocities satisfy the corresponding symmetry conditions. Matching the positions and momenta at two consecutive alignments reduces the computation of RPOs to a low-dimensional nonlinear problem. Its solutions are then numerically continued, and linear stability is determined from the nontrivial eigenvalues of the rotated monodromy matrix after removing the neutral directions associated with conserved quantities and continuous symmetries. The procedure is applied to several mass distributions and initial configurations, producing families of Poincar\'e, Hill, and binary-type solutions. These families exhibit transitions from nearly circular to highly eccentric motion, changes of stability near resonances and turning points, and absolute periodic solutions when the rotation angle is a rational multiple of 2{\pi}. In the Hill families, the continuation connects satellite configurations with circumstellar motion as the smallest body loses its gravitational binding to the intermediate body. Circumbinary and circumstellar configurations are also obtained in the binary regime. The results illustrate the dynamical diversity of RPOs and provide coherent three-body motions that can be used as prescribed trajectories in restricted four-body models.

papers.title: DisCo Algebra: Why Disintegration and Combination Are Not Inverses
papers.abstract: We present DisCo algebra---a compositional framework for joint probability built from a symmetric cooperad (disintegration) and a magma-operad (non-associative partial combination, restricted to the image of disintegration) on the bare family $\mathcal{P}_n=\mathrm{Prob}([0,1]^n)$. No probability integral transform, no external summary functions, no enrichment of objects with conditional kernels. The disintegration side uses block-wise joint CDFs as intrinsic, measure-determined 1D summaries, yielding a lossy compression. The combination side reads the same summaries and reconstructs via regular conditional measures, yielding a lossless embedding on admissible inputs. We prove that combination followed by disintegration is the identity on admissible inputs, but disintegration followed by combination is not---it defines a renormalization operator $R_{\mathcal{I}}=\text{Combine}\circ\text{Disintegrate}$. The information loss of this operator is exactly the probability curvature $\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{I}}(\mu)$---the conditional KL divergence between the true conditional distribution and the conditionally independent product. This curvature measures the obstruction to lossless decomposition and reveals a hard limit on how much cross-block dependence can be captured by CDF-based scalar block summaries.

papers.title: Sharp Quantitative Convergence of Compactly Supported Aggregation-Diffusion
papers.abstract: We establish the quantitative convergence of nonlinear aggregation-diffusion equations in dimension one, with sublinear attraction kernel and degenerate diffusion higher than quadratic. In these models, steady state is known to be the unique, compactly supported, and radial decreasing probability distribution. In this paper, we work with compactly supported densities in dimension one, we prove these solutions converge to the steady state exponentially fast.

papers.title: A spinor-adapted geometric approach to nonlinear Dirac systems on the Schwarzschild black hole background
papers.abstract: Building on our previous work, we extend the spinor-adapted geometric method for nonlinear Dirac systems from small perturbations of Minkowski spacetime to the Schwarzschild background. As a linear foundation, we establish integrated local energy decay estimates and an \(r^p\)-weighted energy hierarchy for spinor fields, adapting the physical-space approach of Dafermos and Rodnianski to the Dirac setting. The main focus of the paper is nonlinear. We consider a semilinear tensorial wave--Dirac model motivated by the wave-gauge reduction of the Einstein--Dirac system and prove global small-data stability. A principal difficulty is the apparent loss of derivatives arising from the coupling between the first-order Dirac equation and the second-order tensorial wave equation. We overcome this difficulty through a spinor-adapted energy hierarchy that exploits the complementary roles of the Dirac-current energy and the spinorial wave energy. In particular, the nonlinear estimates are closed without requiring the top-order Dirac-current estimate. The nonlinear analysis demonstrates that the spinorial structures remain essential on the black-hole background. The combination of Dirac-current energy, spinorial wave energy, Kosmann Lie derivatives, and the Clifford-algebraic null structure enables us to close the nonlinear estimates without imposing an independent null condition on the tensorial wave equation. Thus, the nonlinear closure relies fundamentally on structures intrinsic to the Dirac equation. A second main result is the global small-data stability of the Maxwell--Dirac system in the Lorenz gauge on the Schwarzschild background, under a vanishing-charge assumption. This extends the nonlinear stability theory to a genuine gauge-coupled Dirac system and demonstrates the applicability of the spinor-adapted physical-space approach beyond the tensorial wave--Dirac model.

papers.title: Maximal velocity estimates for Hardy operators
papers.abstract: We prove maximal velocity estimates for the fractional Laplacian with an added subcritical Hardy potential, called Hardy operator, and possibly external potentials. As an application, we give another proof of the nonexistence of the wave operator intertwining Hardy operators with and without long-range perturbations with Coulomb decay.

papers.title: BCC optimality for the three-dimensional Coulomb lattice energy
papers.abstract: We prove that the body-centered cubic lattice uniquely minimizes the renormalized Coulomb energy among three-dimensional Bravais lattices of fixed covolume, up to orthogonal transformations. Using Ewald summation, we write the energy, to within an additive constant, as a sum of two positive, rapidly convergent series in real and reciprocal space. Their positivity provides finite lower bounds for all competitors. A passage to the dual lattice reduces the problem to a face-centered cubic comparison. A short basis vector estimate, a certified local Hessian, and interval bounds on a compact five-dimensional domain complete the computer-assisted proof.

papers.title: The sharp Chern--Simons--Sobolev inequality and its variants
papers.abstract: We introduce and prove a new conformally invariant Chern--Simons--Sobolev inequality, and classify all optimizers, which are the Hopf map $\pi:\mathbb{S}^{2n+1}\to\mathbb{CP}^n$ composed with a symplectic diffeomorphism of $\mathbb{CP}^n$ and an orientation-preserving conformal transformation of $\mathbb{S}^{2n+1}$. The proof uses the sharp curl-Sobolev inequality and a rigidity argument for its equality case. Motivated by the main result, we also introduce the spherical Radu--Tchrakian--Yang functional, and prove the global minimality of the Hopf map for radii in a neighborhood of $((n!)^2/n)^{1/(4n-4)}$, and characterize all minimizers. We also prove local instability for sufficiently small and sufficiently large radii, with explicit lower bounds for the Morse index.

papers.title: Mellin transformed exponential volumes and probabilistic moduli spaces
papers.abstract: A decorated surface is a surface with boundary and a finite set of marked boundary points called cusps. We continue to study the exponential volumes E(S,K,L) of moduli spaces of ideal hyperbolic structures on a decorated surface S, with the given values of lengths of boundary geodesic circles L and boundary geodesic intervals K, introduced in our previous work: 1. We prove that the Mellin--Laplace transform of E(S,K,L) admits Barnes integral presentations, and satisfies recursions, generalising Mirzakhani's recursions. 2. We specify a subset I of the blue boundary intervals, and assign to them any collection of weights. We show that the Mellin transform of the function E(S,K,L) along the variables K at the blue intervals, evaluated at the weights values, calculates weighted exponential volumes of various moduli spaces. If all boundary intervals are blue and all weights are 1/2, we recover Chekhov's volumes of moduli spaces of hyperbolic surfaces with crowns, discretizing the Schwarzian action. We derive recursions for the weighted exponential volumes. 3. We introduce probabilistic Teichmuller spaces related to decorated surfaces S. They are infinite dimensional and carry canonical Wiener type measures. The definition of the measures builds on the works of Bauerschmidt - Losev - Wildemann and Losev. Their quotients by the action of the modular group of S are probabilistic moduli spaces. We show that their volumes are finite. We prove recursion formulas for these measures, and hence for the volumes. The emerging theory generalizes the Schwarzian field theory of Stanford - Witten from the disc to any decorated surfaces, i.e. to open string format. In particular, we get recursions for the Feynman integrals in Schwarzian field theory on decorated surfaces.

papers.title: Widom asymptotics for spatial compressions of Schr\"odinger spectral projections
papers.abstract: We establish a Widom trace formula for spatial compressions of exact spectral projections of semiclassical Schr\"odinger operators. The potential is smooth near a compact classically allowed region, and the observation domain lies strictly inside that region. For every continuous spectral function with positive power decay at both endpoints, we obtain a trace formula at scale $h^{1-n}\log h^{-1}$ whose coefficient separates into a boundary integral and a universal spectral functional. This yields the exact von Neumann and R\'enyi entanglement asymptotics for every fixed positive order, and proves their universal ratios to the particle-number variance. The proof combines commutator estimates in every fixed positive Schatten class with a local trace formula obtained from a boundary-adapted normal form and a Hardy model. In dimensions $n\ge2$, a positive partition and the known variance asymptotic control the grazing contribution; in one dimension all boundary Fermi points are transverse. A harmonic-oscillator counterexample shows that continuity and weighted integrability alone are insufficient for the trace formula.

papers.title: Methods for Deriving Nonlinear Kinetic Equations from the Dynamics of Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: The article outlines key topics related to deriving kinetic equations and, in general, to the relationship between the evolution equations governing quantum many-particle systems. The main issues being considered are the mathematical origin of quantum kinetic equations, novel methods for deriving kinetic equations from hierarchies of evolution equations for quantum systems, specifically focusing on kinetics within the framework of the evolution of observables, and the generalization of the quantum kinetic equation specified by non-separable initial states.

papers.title: The Octonionic Rational Wave Numbers: Non-Associative Sequence Algebras, Moufang Loops, and Exceptional $G_2$ Symmetries
papers.abstract: We generalize discrete rational wave numbers (arXiv:2609.23233) to the octonionic rational wave numbers $\mathbb{O}^\mathbb{Z}$ over Cayley's octonions $\mathbb{O}$. Rather than assuming higher imaginary units, all rational wave number spaces $\mathbb{C}^\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{H}^\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{O}^\mathbb{Z}$ are derived constructively from two scalar primitives: the coordinate advance $E_Z$ and phase calibration $E_{\bar{1}}$. Their closure under pointwise multiplication, inversion, and rational roots generates an infinite divisible Moufang loop on the sequence ring $\mathcal{S}_\mathbb{O} := \mathbb{O}^\mathbb{Z}$, terminating strictly at $\mathbb{O}^\mathbb{Z}$ via sedenionic zero-divisor excision. By Artin's Theorem, pairwise compositions remain strictly associative, whereas three-wave interactions generate an intrinsic non-associative curvature quantified by the associator $[u, v, w] = (uv)w - u(vw)$. We define a real-valued sequence inner product that bypasses the Jordan--von Neumann--Wigner obstruction, establishing the orthonormality of the seven Fano coordinate primitives. We establish three principal theorems: (1) The Invariant Hexagonal Mesh Theorem, proving that cumulative integration exhibits a scale-invariant bifurcation at $n=6$ governed by the root system of $G_2 = \operatorname{Aut}(\mathbb{O})$ and its $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ stabilizer subgroup; (2) The Algebraic Phase Jitter Theorem, showing that Catalan parenthesization trees across non-Fano triads produce an irreducible zero-point phase fluctuation, yielding an algebraic origin for vacuum jitter; and (3) The Rational Loop Closure Theorem, proving that rational frequencies select closed finite Moufang sub-loops, while irrational frequencies yield topologically dense, non-closing trajectories. This provides an autonomous, discrete algebraic foundation for non-associative geometry and fundamental physical symmetries.

papers.title: Lieb-Robinson bounds via the Combes-Thomas estimate
papers.abstract: This paper studies quantum spin systems: networks of spins coupled by local interactions. The Lieb-Robinson bound predicts that in these systems, information propagates at an essentially finite speed. We produce a new proof of this result. Our approach relies on a spectral bound on entries of resolvents of band matrices, the Combes-Thomas estimate, rather than on the standard path-counting argument.

papers.title: On the Road Again: How the $N$-Lane TASEP and Local Reservoirs Drive Jamming in Axonal Transport
papers.abstract: Intracellular transport by molecular motors along microtubules is essential for cellular function, particularly in neuronal axons where track disruption drives neurodegenerative disease. We develop an \(N\)-track totally asymmetric simple exclusion process (TASEP) model where motors reversibly detach into local off-track states. Using mean-field, continuum, and fast-switching approximations, we derive an effective nonlinear transport equation for total motor density. This reduced model retains the classical TASEP phase structure but reveals that increasing \(N\) shifts the boundaries between low-density, high-density, and maximal-current regimes. Crucially, under source-driven boundary conditions reflecting constant cargo production, the entrance density undergoes a saddle-node bifurcation when the production rate exceeds the network's transport capacity, \(N/4\). This triggers persistent cargo accumulation that propagates throughout the domain. Our results establish a physical mechanism by which gradual microtubule degradation drives a transition from efficient transport to jammed pathological states.

papers.title: The L\'{e}vy wave packet and fractional uncertainty relations
papers.abstract: This work revisits the debate on fractional uncertainty relations that arose a decade ago and tries to settle it. After a careful study of the position-momentum uncertainty product of the L\'{e}vy wave packet, a novel lower bound is proposed for uncertainty relations in fractional quantum mechanics. This bound is nearly linear in the L\'{e}vy index and is satisfied by exact, calculable solutions available in the literature.

papers.title: Geometrization of continuum mechanics and nonequilibrium thermodynamics: Heat conduction
papers.abstract: We propose a geometric formulation of non-equilibrium heat conduction. It combines the variational (Hamiltonian) structure of symmetric hyperbolic thermodynamically compatible (SHTC) equations with the exterior calculus of differential forms. The central object is the thermal impulse one-form on the four-dimensional matter-time manifold. Its time component is the temperature, and for reversible (ballistic) heat transport it is the exact differential of a scalar potential (i.e. it is holonomic). Non-equilibrium effects are described by a second one-form, the small-scale thermal impulse, which is not required to be exact. Its time component is a fluctuating temperature, and its exterior derivative, the four-thermal vorticity, satisfies a Bianchi-type kinematic identity. The variational principle together with this identity yields a non-equilibrium two-temperature model. Its field equations have the same structure as Maxwell's equations in a medium, with the thermal impulse field, the thermal vorticity field and a thermal Poynting vector contributing to the heat flux. Dissipation is introduced through relaxation terms that conserve the total energy and produce entropy. A formal asymptotic analysis shows that, in the relaxation limit, the model reduces to a Guyer-Krumhansl-type heat conduction with independent transverse and longitudinal length scales. The transverse nonlocal term comes from the spatial non-holonomy of the small-scale thermal impulse, while the longitudinal term comes from its non-holonomy in time, i.e. from the relaxation of the fluctuating temperature. We also discuss the gauge-theoretic interpretation of the model. Its kinematics is that of an abelian gauge theory, while the local gauge symmetry is explicitly broken by the existence of two temperatures. Finally, we discuss the consequences of the geometric structure for structure-preserving numerical methods.

papers.title: On the planar Neumann--Poincar\'e inverse spectral problem
papers.abstract: Does the Neumann--Poincar\'e spectrum determine a planar domain up to an extended M\"obius transformation? We construct a pair showing that the answer is no, even for analytic, strictly convex, algebraic boundaries. Their operators are similar. We then prove a positive result for prescribed finite-dimensional families of normalised exterior conformal maps. For every $m\ge1$, the first $m$ positive eigenvalues determine $m$ real Laurent coefficients on a small truncated convex cone, provided the higher coefficients are a prescribed analytic remainder of quadratic order. Recovery is Lipschitz stable, uniformly down to the disk. The proof combines the Grunsky representation with a nondegeneracy argument for weighted Hankel matrices and differentiated perturbation estimates. Explicit two- and three-parameter examples, single-mode families with repeated leading eigenvalues, and M\"obius equivalence classes illustrate the result. Direct proofs for complete polarization data show what spectral weights add to the eigenvalues.

papers.title: Quantum Charge as a Particle/Antiparticle Label
papers.abstract: We show that the concept of particles and antiparticles is related to the Weyl-Heisenberg group $W\!H_3$. Its generators are the position operators $\hat x^a$, the momentum operators $\hat p_a$, and the central element $Q_{\sf{v}}$, which defines a subgroup U(1)$_{\sf v}$ of $W\!H_3$. We show that the wave functions have a charge relative to the group U(1)$_{\sf{v}}$ equal to either $q_+=1/\hbar$ (particle $\psi_+$) or $q_-=-1/\hbar$ (antiparticle $\psi_-$). We call these eigenvalues of the operator $Q_{\sf{v}}$ quantum charges: $Q_{\sf{v}}\psi_\pm^{}=q_\pm^{}\psi_\pm^{}$. The wave functions $\psi_+$ and $\psi_-$ belong to the Hilbert spaces $\mathcal{H}_+$ and $\mathcal{H}_-$, on which unitarily inequivalent representations $\pi_\hbar$ and $\pi_{-\hbar}$ of the Weyl-Heisenberg group $W\!H_3$ are defined. These representations are related to each other by the antilinear charge conjugation operator $\hat C$, which maps $\mathcal{H}_+, q_+$ to $\mathcal{H}_-, q_-$. Charges $q_\pm^{}$ are intrinsic characteristics of the wave functions $\psi_\pm^{}$, similar to spin and electric charge. The wave function possesses one of these charges, $q_+$ or $q_-$, prior to the specification of any equations. We show that negative probabilities/energies and the Klein paradox in Klein-Gordon and Dirac theories are consequences of the violation of U(1)$_{\sf v}$-invariance in these theories. Restoring this invariance separates particle and antiparticles and eliminates all paradoxes at the level of first-quantized relativistic theories.

papers.title: Generalized Coordinate Bethe Ansatz and Quantum Integrability of the Time-Dependent Massive Thirring Model
papers.abstract: We develop a generalized coordinate Bethe-ansatz framework for the massive Thirring model with an explicitly time-dependent fermion mass. Unlike the generalized Bethe ansatz for chiral quantum field theories, where particle transport acts in internal spin spaces and leads to quantum Knizhnik-Zamolodchikov equations, the present construction acts directly on particle coordinates and physical rapidities. Its central new feature is a rapidity lattice. Because the time-dependent mass couples right- and left-moving components already in the one-particle sector, a fixed-rapidity block is not closed under spatial winding. Periodicity therefore requires all sectors generated by the finite shift $\beta\to\beta-p$. Particle exchange relates amplitudes on this lattice through scalar analytic difference equations of Ruijsenaars type, whose solutions determine the complete time-dependent many-body wavefunction. Consistency of the coordinate construction also selects an exponential evolution of the bare mass, providing a new realization of the time dependent integrability-renormalization group correspondence. In the static limit, the rapidity-lattice construction reduces to the conventional massive-Thirring Bethe equations. Through the massive-Thirring/sine Gordon equivalence, the result also connects this exact quantum construction to the generalized space-time dependent Lax formalism.

papers.title: Percolation on Bidirected Graphs
papers.abstract: We study bidirected percolation on an undirected graph $G$: each edge is replaced by two oppositely directed edges, each of which is open independently with probability $p$. Two vertices are strongly connected if they are mutually reachable by open directed paths. Let $p_\mathrm{sc}$ denote the threshold for the existence of an infinite strongly connected cluster, and let $p_c$ denote the usual Bernoulli percolation threshold on $G$. On every transitive amenable graph, we prove that $p_\mathrm{sc}=p_c$. In contrast, sufficiently spread-out modifications of every transitive non-amenable graph satisfy $p_\mathrm{sc}>p_c$. We also show that, on $\mathbb Z^d$ with $d\ge11$, the expected size of the strongly connected cluster is finite at $p=p_\mathrm{sc}$.

papers.title: The Prevalence of Straight Shots in Control Space for Reaching Optimal Quantum Performance
papers.abstract: Gradient-based algorithms are often applied to identify an optimal control for maximizing a quantum objective functional by following a steepest ascent path to the top of the control landscape. In contrast, this paper explores straight shots through control space where movement along such a path corresponds to a less demanding monotonic complete climb up the landscape for the optimal objective value. Existing studies of control landscapes have revealed the presence of straight shots, but identifying them required computationally intensive stochastic methods. In this paper, we introduce a non-stochastic straight-shot search algorithm (STSA) that identifies a large class of straight shots. We apply STSA to numerically generate more than 10,000 distinct straight-shot optimization paths and analyze their statistical distribution for each of the objectives of (i) state-to-state transitions, (ii) general observables, and (iii) unitary transformation generation. The results show a decrease in the nearest-neighbor distances among straight shots as the sample size increases, suggesting their prevalence in control space. We further conjecture that the starting locations of the straight-shot pathways on a landscape level set may form connected neighborhoods, motivating future investigation into their underlying topological structure. The present paper focuses on the use of STSA for locating massive numbers of straight solutions. However, the STSA is not a high-efficiency algorithm in its present form, but the discovered prevalence of control straight shots leaves open future advances to accelerate the discovery of straight shots as optimal controls.

papers.title: "Massive" Conformal Field Theories and application to Nambu-Goto string
papers.abstract: I describe the recent progress in understanding diffeomorphism invariant two-dimensional theories with dimensionful parameters which have nevertheless traceless improved energy-momentum tensor and turn out to be conformal invariant. An example is the Liouville theory with the additional four-derivative terms arising from the Nambu-Goto string and telling apart the Nambu-Goto and Polyakov strings. Its exact solution in embedding dimension d=4 is consistent in contrast to the Polyakov string and described by the (4,3) unitary minimal model. Talk at Irina Aref'eva Conference "Perspective Directions in Quantum Field Theory and Superstrings", Moscow 12-17 October 2026.

papers.title: Adapted Fr\"ohlich-Pizzo Model for Horizon-Induced Decoherence
papers.abstract: The Fr\"ohlich-Pizzo (FP) model is a quantum-mechanical model originally developed to describe the interaction between an atom and the electromagnetic field in the nonrelativistic limit $c\to\infty$. We show that an adaptation of the FP model based on the local algebras of a $U(1)$ chiral current captures essential features of the horizon-induced decoherence mechanism identified by Danielson, Satishchandran, and Wald (DSW) in the limit of large holding time $T$. Our analysis suggests that the effective dynamics of the system undergoing decoherence in the DSW setting retains non-Markovian features. Our approach also offers a glimpse into the possible role of quantum events in the dynamics underlying horizon-induced decoherence.

papers.title: Stochastic resonance in time-delayed bistable active particles
papers.abstract: We investigate analytically and numerically stochastic resonance in an underdamped active (Ornstein--Uhlenbeck) particle confined in a bistable potential with time-delayed feedback and subjected to an additional (non-thermal) white-noise source. Restricting the analysis to the active-noise-dominated bistable regime, with sufficiently short delay and active-noise correlation times, we develop a perturbative theory that yields analytical expressions for both the escape rate and the spectral power amplification within the framework of linear-response theory, without invoking detailed balance. The analytical predictions are in qualitative agreement with direct numerical simulations throughout the perturbative regime. We show that a moderate increase in the active-noise correlation time can enhance the stochastic-resonance response, in marked contrast to previous results for overdamped passive systems driven by colored noise. Conversely, the addition of white noise weakens the resonant response and shifts its optimum toward lower active-noise intensities. Time-delayed feedback further alters the matching condition between the escape rate and the driving frequency while preserving the resonant mechanism. Beyond the perturbative regime, we find that finite-memory effects progressively broaden the resonance profile and substantially decrease its amplitude. Overall, these results provide new insight into the combined role of inertia, activity, environmental fluctuations, and time delayed feedback in stochastic resonance in nonequilibrium systems.

papers.title: Fermion-Number Variation for Several Coupling Schemes in an $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ Chiral Soliton Background
papers.abstract: When topological solitons are coupled to fermions, they often induce a nontrivial fermion number. In the chiral quark soliton model (CQSM), this phenomenon underlies the identification of soliton topology with baryon number. However, whether this topology--fermion-number correspondence is determined solely by soliton topology or also depends on the fermion--soliton coupling scheme remains unclear. In this paper, we investigate this question by comparing several coupling schemes to the same $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ chiral soliton background. To treat the corresponding Dirac Hamiltonians within a common framework, we evaluate the variation of the regularized fermion-number along a model-parameter space. For the standard chiral Yukawa coupling of the CQSM, this variation reproduces the topological charge $Q$ associated with $\pi_3(\mathrm{SU}(N))$. The same result is obtained for an axial-vector coupling, whereas the fermion number variation vanishes for a vector coupling, despite the nontrivial topology of the chiral soliton background. These results provide an explicit example in which soliton topology alone does not determine the fermionic response; the topology--fermion-number correspondence also depends on how the background field is coupled to fermions.

papers.title: On unitary vertex operator algebras
papers.abstract: We prove that a conformal vertex algebra with a non-zero invariant Hermitian form is unitary as soon as it admits a non-zero positive energy module with a positive definite invariant Hermitian form. Using free field realizations, we deduce that the principal simple $W$-algebra $W_k(\mathfrak g)$ of a simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ is unitary for central charge $c\ge rank(\mathfrak g)+24\bigl((\rho|\rho^\vee)+\|\rho\|\,\|\rho^\vee\|\bigr)$, and, if $\mathfrak g$ is simply laced, for all $c\ge rank(\mathfrak g)$. Among basic Lie superalgebras which are not Lie algebras, the free field argument applies to $osp(1|2n)$ and $osp(2|2n)$. It shows that $W_k(osp(1|2n))$ is unitary for $c\ge n+\frac12$ and gives an explicit bound for $osp(2|2n)$. Next, we prove that if $\mathfrak s$ is an even $sl_2$-subalgebra of a simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ whose centralizer is not abelian, then the simple $W$-algebra $W_k(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak s)$ is unitary for at most finitely many $k$. We illustrate this on the $W$-algebras of $sl_{qm}$ attached to the nilpotents of Jordan type $q^m$: unitarity is possible only at two levels, and for $q=2$ it does occur at both. For instance, the $W$-algebra of $sl_4$ attached to the partition $2+2$ is unitary only for $k=-2$ and $k=-\frac32$. This fails for Lie superalgebras, as minimal $W$-algebras show, but still holds under stronger assumptions. Finally, we prove that a simple $W$-algebra $W_k(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak s)$ can be unitary for only finitely many $k$ if $\mathfrak g$ is a simple Lie algebra and $\mathfrak s$ is not a distinguished $sl_2$ subalgebra.

papers.title: Painlev\'e representations for joint moments of characteristic polynomials from the orthogonal and unitary symplectic groups
papers.abstract: We study joint moments of characteristic polynomials and their second derivatives for Haar-distributed matrices from the unitary symplectic and orthogonal groups. We establish their large-$N$ asymptotics throughout the full admissible range of the moment parameters and identify the limiting coefficients probabilistically in terms of the first inverse power sum of the Bessel point process. This extends the corresponding results of Assiotis, Gunes, Keating, and Wei [Proc. Lond. Math. Soc., 132 (2026), e70136] to the full admissible parameter range. Throughout this full range, we also express these limits in terms of a distinguished solution of the $\sigma$-Painlev\'e III' equation. Our approach reduces the problem to singular inverse-power statistics of the Jacobi unitary ensemble and combines their finite-$N$ $\sigma$-Painlev\'e V representation with a refined Riemann-Hilbert analysis yielding precise small-$x$ asymptotics and uniform derivative estimates for the finite-$N$ correction term. A key ingredient in the probabilistic identification is a kernel-based proof that the rescaled first inverse power sum of the Jacobi ensemble converges in distribution to its Bessel point process counterpart.

papers.title: Finite Classification of Transversal Diagonal Gates Beyond Stabilizer Codes
papers.abstract: We establish that transversal diagonal gates on exact qubit codes of distance at least two can be exhaustively classified within a finite search space. Although code-preserving physical gates can have continuous phases, any projective logical action induced by a transversal diagonal gate can always be realized by a physical gate of finite order. Crucially, we prove that this physical order has an upper bound determined solely by the code parameters. This order bound enables the subset-sum-linear-programming (SSLP) framework introduced in arXiv:2504.20847 to exhaustively enumerate all candidate discrete symmetries, after which the Knill-Laflamme equations determine the remaining continuous code parameters. Applying this method to the nontrivial diagonal sector of exact $((6,2,3))$ codes, SSLP yields $66$ candidate symmetry classes, of which exactly $15$ are realizable, supporting full projective diagonal logical cyclic groups of orders $2$, $3$, and $5$. In particular, for order $5$, the code is unique up to local unitaries and qubit permutations, equivalent to the code constructed in arXiv:2504.20847. This code also attains the minimum length $n=6$ among exact $((n, 2, \ge 3))$ codes whose full projective transversal group cannot be conjugated into the projective Clifford group.
